messages:
emily (Support): FYI customer AcmeGames just hit 429s during a live demo. They were on free-tier trying to spin up a chat demo for investors. They say it started ~10:12am PST and persisted for ~8 minutes. Requesting: can we grant a short burst or clarify upgrade path?

Details I have:
- Customer account id: acct_01G5ZX7
- Public demo key used: pk_demo_ggXYZ (they used this in prod by mistake)
- Repro steps they gave:
  1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer pk_demo_ggXYZ" -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"demo"},{"role":"user","content":"start"}]}'
  2) spawn 15 concurrent clients (they used a small k6 script)
- Error seen: 429 with body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":30} and occasional 502/504 on the gateway
- Customer also reported one auth failure earlier: 401 with message "invalid api key" (they rotated keys mid-demo)

Can SRE confirm whether this is pure quota exhaustion or if the gateway mis-routed them to a lower-tier pool? Also need billing/sales to advise on quick upgrade + any temporary grace window.

luis (Billing): Thanks Emily. I pulled acct_01G5ZX7 — they are on free-tier (cap: 60 requests/minute per api key; 120k tokens/month). The demo key pk_demo_ggXYZ is flagged as "public demo" on our side which gets an additional safety throttle of 2x to avoid abuse, but concurrency is still limited. From the usage logs: they peaked at ~520 req/min for the demo window, which triggered hard 429s.

We can issue a manual temporary burst (account-level) for up to 24 hours. Options:
- soft bump to 300 req/min for 24h (no invoice)
- temp trial of paid tier (Pro) for 7 days with $0 charge, requires sales approval + quick TOS acknowledgement

If we do a manual bump, we need to whitelist their demo src IPs or the key id to avoid cascading to other accounts. What does SRE need to safely increase?

tom (SRE): Repro and notes:
- I checked rate-limiter logs and saw their key id hitting token bucket exhaustion across two frontends. The routing correctly put them on the free-tier pool; no fallback to dedicated.
- The 502/504s correlate with a short-lived spike in upstream latency (model worker queue grew) when bursts hit. Not a platform outage, but the queue backpressure caused gateway timeouts.
- Auth 401 event: looks like they swapped to a rotated key mid-run; that explains the early 401 then subsequent valid requests. Recommend customers rotate keys out of peak windows.

Quick safe steps if we want to allow the demo to finish:
1) luis: manual account-level burst to 300 req/min for 24h (I can add an enforcement flag to bypass per-key demo throttle).
2) I will pin their traffic to a larger pool instance and raise worker concurrency for that pool (+15%) for the next 2 hours.
3) ask the customer to add header x-demo=true so we can filter their traffic and revert after window.

Technical note (for ops): example command to inspect logs by request id:
```
# search gateway logs for account
rg "acct_01G5ZX7" /var/log/gateway/* | tail -n 200
# get request trace
curl -H "X-Request-ID: <id>" https://internal-logs/api/trace/<id>
```
jess (Sales): I can own the handoff. If they want to go paid after the demo: Pro plan includes 1M tokens/mo and 2x baseline throughput; we can offer a 30% first-quarter credit for demo customers converting within 14 days. For an immediate unblock I recommend the 24h manual bump + a 14-day trial of Pro. If they accept trial, I need contact + company billing PO to set up.

Two process questions:
- do we require a signed trial agreement for a 7d pro trial with $0 charge? (we sometimes do SOC/legal checks)
- what's the manual-bump audit trail? we need to record the change for compliance.

luis (Billing): No signed agreement required for 7d trial $0 charge — standard internal SKU. I'll create a billing ticket and set the trial flag if we get verbal ok. Audit trail: I will log the manual quota change in billing-ops and tag the ticket with who approved and the reason.

emily (Support): Customer just replied: "We can do the 24h bump and the 14-day trial, please make it so — demo ends tomorrow 5pm PST." They gave a list of three IPs: 3.8.22.10, 18.223.1.9, 35.90.12.5.

tom (SRE): Ok I can pin IP whitelist + bump. Two quick notes:
- Whitelisting IPs at the edge will bypass some of our public demo protections; only whitelist specific key ids + IPs together. Please confirm the exact header/key they will use.
- I'll coordinate a short firewall rule change: change will be in 2-phase (apply, validate, revert if error).

ratebot: Automatic alert: spike detected — acct_01G5ZX7 exceeded 5x baseline for 00:07:34, generated 412 429 responses. Ticket created: #SUP-48291.

jess (Sales): Emily, please DM me customer billing contact + legal contact. I'll draft trial terms and allocate a sales rep for upsell followup.

luis (Billing): I created billing ticket BK-9931 and set temporary stake for manual-bump. Approval required from one of: jess or finance-lead. jess, pls ack here and I'll apply.

jess (Sales): Ack. Apply the 24h 300req/min bump. Put trial start = now, trial length = 14 days zero-dollar. Include note: "demo uplift approved per Sales (jess) - AcmeGames"

tom (SRE): Done on my side: pinned traffic, increased worker concurrency for pool free-tier-1 by +20%, added IP-key whitelist for provided IPs + pk_demo_ggXYZ, and monitored latency. I left a revert timer scheduled for 24h. Observed immediate reduction in 429s; they now sustain ~280 req/min without 502s.

emily (Support): Customer confirms demo resumed and is stable. They also asked about a future-proof upgrade path—can Sales share the exact steps and an approximate time to provision Dedicated capacity if they convert?

jess (Sales): Standard upgrade steps:
1) sign invoice / accept trial -> provision Pro within 1 hour (self-serve for most accounts)
2) for Dedicated: needs capacity planning + PO, typically 3-5 business days + infra approval. We can fast-track to 48-72 hours if they commit to monthly reserved capacity.

emily (Support): Great. I'll close the thread after the revert timer fires and we confirm normal queues. Thanks everyone. :tada:

tom (SRE): Please remind customer to rotate their demo key outside demo windows and to use short-lived keys for public demos. Also recommend adding exponential backoff on client side to avoid synchronized retries.

luis (Billing): I'll attach BK-9931 to SUP-48291 and mark billing action complete after revert.

ratebot: Note: manual-bump audit log -> admin: luis, request: SUP-48291, change: +240 req/min, duration: 24h, time: 1912340200

emily (Support): Closing notes: action items for post-mortem: 1) update support KB on "demo best practices" (Emily), 2) add a short-run playbook for manual-bump (Tom + Luis), 3) Sales follow-up plan (Jess).
